document: The executable closure of the M5 PostgreSQL upgrade campaign
note: The single source of truth for what the upgrade campaign is made of. The producer reads it to record the object identity of every path at the tree it actually ran on; the verifier reads it to require those identities to still hold. Neither restates the list, because a list kept in two places is a list that will disagree.
rule: A change to anything here changes what the evidence is evidence of, so retained reports produced before the change may not be promoted after it: the campaign has to be run again. A change to anything not here — documentation, the changelog, or unrelated jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — leaves retained evidence valid. The dedicated `.github/workflows/m5-upgrade.yml` is bound as one object, so changes to the upgrade provisioning or call layer invalidate upgrade evidence without binding the rest of CI.
historical_revision_note: The rejection report builds a real schema-2 runtime from `SCHEMA2_RUNTIME_REVISION` in `crates/oxide-batch/tests/upgrade/mod.rs`, checked out into a worktree at run time — it is a revision identifier, not a path, so it cannot itself be an object this closure hashes. What the closure binds instead is the file that names it: a change to that constant, or to the matching `schema2_runtime.revision` field in campaign-scope.json, changes the object identity of a path already listed under campaign fixtures or campaign implementation below, which invalidates retained evidence the same as any other semantic change. crates/oxide-batch/tests/m5_upgrade_campaign.rs additionally asserts in review that the two values are byte-identical, so the two files cannot drift from each other unnoticed even before a campaign run would catch it.

workspace framework and adapter source.why: Every report runs the runtime and the PostgreSQL adapter this code declares — the migrator, the repository and explorer ports, and the newer-schema rejection the current runtime enforces on the rollback report's restored databases.

migrations.why: The immutable migration set every report installs a prior schema from and upgrades through. Schema 1 and schema 2 are the schema this set produced when it was the whole set, not a fixture wearing an older number, and the upgrade path under test is the real remaining chain.

campaign implementation.why: The exact test targets the committed scope document's reports name, plus the shared support module those targets compile against — which also carries the pinned SCHEMA2_RUNTIME_REVISION the rejection report builds its historical runtime from. A workspace test file not listed here is outside the campaign: it is not selected, so it is neither run nor able to affect the campaign's result.

cargo manifests.why: Feature selection and dependency ranges for every crate the campaign builds and runs. A campaign built with different features is a different campaign.

dependency resolution.why: The exact dependency graph every target the campaign runs was built from, including the historical schema-2 runtime, which is built with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pointed outside its worktree but resolves against the same lockfile.

toolchain and build configuration.why: The compiler the campaign, and the historical schema-2 runtime, are built with, and the cargo configuration they are built under.

campaign fixtures.why: The declared denominator — the two prior-schema sources, the three reports, the five schema paths, and the pinned schema-2 runtime revision — and this closure itself. The producer derives what it runs and what each report must observe from this document, and the historical-schema seed scripts are the committed fixtures a source schema is populated with before the upgrade under test runs.

upgrade execution contract.why: How CI actually runs the campaign: the supported matrix, the database and maintenance connection it is given, the command, the environment, and the full-history checkout the historical schema-2 runtime worktree requires. The dedicated workflow is included with them, and its contract-check step fails closed if the workflow drifts from the contract. An unrelated CI job in ci.yml does not invalidate retained upgrade evidence, while any change to the dedicated upgrade workflow does.

independent verifier.why: The program that decides whether a run proved what it owed and whether retained evidence is still what it says. Its verdicts are part of the campaign result, so a report produced under a different verifier is a result under a different standard. Listed as the specific files that implement it, matching the soak, cancellation, performance, conformance, and crash-restore campaigns' own closures: `main.rs` dispatches the command, `upgrade.rs` runs the scope and reconciles the observations against it, `evidence.rs` is the permanent offline verifier, and `suite.rs` is the target-running and libtest-parsing mechanics every M5 runner shares.
